newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais seek to be financial hub despite controls.
newsitem.headline: Thais seek to be financial hub despite controls.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Thursday that the government still wanted to promote Thailand as a financial centre despite recent currency control measures to curb baht supply to speculators.
"The recent measures don't mean the government has scrapped plans to promote Thailand as a financial centre," Amnuay told reporters.
"But they are aimed at preventing any speculation against the baht," he said.

The Bank of Thailand launched currency controls in mid-May to strike back at speculators after their latest attack on the embattled currency. It cut off baht supplies from local sources to foreign speculators.
The Bank of Thailand said on Wednesday that it would soon formalise currency controls imposed since last month to beat off baht predators.
The central bank earlier this week also implemented new measures aimed at curbing foreigners from repatriating baht funds raised through the stock market.
Analysts had said the measures would obstruct Thailand's plan to become a financial centre and to promote the baht as a regional currency.
